entry.title: SAP Cloud ALM | Implementation | CDM | SAP Launchpad Application
entry.content:
In a SAP Cloud ALM tenant, one of the landscapes has been set up with the change and deployment management module to manage transport requirements for SAP S4HANA, SAP CPI systems, and the SAP launchpad system. 

 

For above mentioned CPI and Launchpad system, the SAP cloud transport management system (CTMS) is already integrated into the SAP cloud alm tool via the SAP BTP cockpit.

CTS is enabled for S4HANA system.

 

I can view all the systems of above-mentioned sap applications in the landscape management of SAP cloud ALM administration Console. 

 

The system groups and deployment plans are in place. In system group for launchpad system we have tried with two products as SAP BTP cloud foundry environment  and SAP build work zone, standard edition

For the  SAP CPI we have selected product as SAP integration suite.

 

We can create features and add transport for the S/4HANA and CPI systems in the Features app.

However, when adding transport for the Launchpad system and selecting the 'Assign' button in the Features app, none of the transports of  Launchpad systems are getting listed. Rest of the systems S4HANA and CPI are listed, but the Launchpad system is not.  

 

Checked following :

Flag of “controlled by Solution Manager” is not set for Dev and UAT system, though for the prod system is set, but as of now not able to view the Dev or UAT in the list while assigning the transport.

Same CTMS is already leveraged for CPI systems, and no issues are observed nor encounter any errors for CPI transports.

In LMS of Cloud ALM, the attempt to create endpoint creation is throwing error stating endpoint creation is not required for SAP build work zone standard edition as none of the CALM use cases requires endpoint.

entry.title: Unexpected Connections Consumption in SAP Build Work Zone Standard Edition
entry.content:
Hello SAP Community,

We are currently implementing a Supplier Portal using SAP Build Work Zone, Standard Edition.

Our current subscription includes:

1,000 Active Users
0 Connections

Authentication is performed through SAP Cloud Identity Services (Identity Authentication - IAS) as our Identity Provider (IdP).

Due to an omission during the commercial contracting process, our subscription was provisioned with Active Users only, while the Connections metric was not included. We are already discussing this situation with our SAP Account Team, but we would like to better understand both the technical behavior and whether anyone has experienced a similar situation.

During our testing, we observed that every external login generates Connections, even though our subscription does not include this metric.

From a technical perspective, we would like to know:

1. Is the generation of the Connections metric mandatory in SAP Build Work Zone Standard Edition?
2. Is there any way to completely prevent the generation of the Connections metric through Role Collections, authorizations or SAP Build Work Zone configuration?

From a commercial perspective, we would also appreciate guidance from anyone who has experienced a similar situation.

Any guidance or shared experience would be greatly appreciated.

Thank you.

entry.title: SAP Build Work Zone Licensing vs HTML5 Application Repository for External Users
entry.content:
We are currently using SAP Build Work Zone to provide access to our SAPUI5 application. However, we have observed a very high consumption of Connections from external users, which has significantly increased our licensing costs.

As an alternative, we are evaluating an architecture where the SAPUI5 application is hosted in the HTML5 Application Repository and accessed through a custom AppRouter, without using SAP Build Work Zone.

In this scenario:

  • Would access to the application still generate SAP Build Work Zone licensing consumption (such as Connections or Active Users)?
  • If not, which SAP BTP services and metrics would be considered for billing instead?
  • Is using the HTML5 Application Repository without SAP Build Work Zone a recommended approach for reducing licensing costs in scenarios with a large number of external users?

We have reviewed the available SAP documentation, but it is not entirely clear how licensing and billing behave in this specific architecture.

Any clarification, documentation references, or recommendations from SAP or the community would be greatly appreciated.

entry.title: Does Accessing Applications Hosted in HTML5 Application Repository Incur Costs?
entry.content:
We are trying to better understand the licensing model for applications hosted in the HTML5 Application Repository.

Does accessing an application deployed in the HTML5 Application Repository generate any licensing or usage charges by itself?

If so:

  • Which SAP BTP service is responsible for the billing?
  • How is the usage measured (e.g., requests, active users, connections, storage, runtime, etc.)?
  • Is there any difference in the billing model when the application is accessed through a custom AppRouter instead of SAP Build Work Zone?

The reason for this question is that we are evaluating replacing SAP Build Work Zone due to the high licensing costs associated with external user connections. We would like to understand whether using the HTML5 Application Repository directly would avoid those charges or simply shift the costs to another BTP service.

Any clarification or references to the official SAP documentation would be greatly appreciated.

entry.title: Joule + M365 Copilot (Teams): can standard transactions run, and are custom Skills / Agent Gateway r
entry.content:
Situation

Following the SAP Help Portal guide "Using Joule with Microsoft 365 Copilot," I integrated Joule with Microsoft 365 Copilot (Teams) and can use Joule from Teams. Q&A works, but transactional requests (e.g., viewing a sales order) do not: Joule replies that, due to system limitations, it cannot access real-time data / APIs and offers manual steps instead. The same happens in the Joule Web Client (Fiori) as well.

Viewing sales orders is listed as a standard Joule transactional capability (Viewing Business Data), yet it won't execute — even after I confirmed the integration, content sync, and the required display authorizations are all in place.

Questions

  1. Standard transactions like viewing sales orders are officially supported, so does this response mean the capability just isn't activated in this landscape? If so, what is needed to enable transactional execution here?
  2. Through the Teams / M365 Copilot integration, are only built-in capabilities available, or can custom Skills / Agents built in Joule Studio also be triggered from Teams? (Microsoft's docs say Copilot Studio custom agents aren't routed, but it's unclear whether Joule Studio ones are.)
  3. If custom transactional Skills / Agents can't be triggered via the Teams add-in, what's the recommended way to launch them from Teams (e.g., via Agent Gateway, once available)?

Environment

SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition; Joule × M365 Copilot (Teams) and Joule Web Client (Fiori); auth via Microsoft Entra ID ⇔ SAP Cloud Identity Services (IAS).

entry.title: Guidance Required End to End Supplier Invoice Automation in SAP S/4HANA Public
entry.content:
Hello Experts,

I am new to the SAP Automation domain and would appreciate your guidance on an end to end Supplier Invoice Automation scenario in SAP S/4HANA Public Cloud using SAP Build Process Automation.

I am currently working on a project with the following business requirement :-

  • A supplier invoice is received as an email in Microsoft Outlook.
  • The automation monitors the mailbox and retrieves the incoming email.
  • The attached PDF invoice is downloaded.
  • The invoice data is extracted using SAP Document AI.
  • The extracted data is validated and used to create a Supplier Invoice in SAP S/4HANA Public Cloud.
  • After the Supplier Invoice is created successfully, the downloaded PDF should be attached to the created Supplier Invoice as a supporting document.
  • After successful processing, the email is marked as Completed in Outlook.

I have attached the automation flow for reference, which represents the expected business process.

I have already completed the prerequisite configuration, including :-

  • SAP BTP account setup
  • Subscription to SAP Build Process Automation
  • Required communication arrangements in SAP S/4HANA Public Cloud
  • Creation of the Supplier Invoice Automation project

At this stage, I need guidance on designing the complete workflow, especially :-

  • Connecting to Outlook and monitoring incoming emails
  • Downloading PDF attachments
  • Configuring SAP Document AI extraction
  • Mapping the extracted fields to the Supplier Invoice API
  • Creating the Supplier Invoice in SAP S/4HANA Public Cloud
  • Attaching the downloaded PDF to the created Supplier Invoice
  • Marking as completed or moving it to Complete folder in Outlook

Please find the API details attached for your reference, as this is the API we are using in the automation process.

  • API_SUPPLIERINVOICE_PROCESS_SRV = (Used to create the Supplier Invoice).
  • API_CV_ATTACHMENT_SRV = (Used to attach the supporting document (PDF) to the created Supplier Invoice).

Could anyone share any official documentation, blogs, tutorials, or step by step implementation guides for this complete scenario?

Any guidance or learning resources would be greatly appreciated.

Thank you.

entry.title: SAP Build Work Zone Standard Edition Subscription Fails with IAS POST 403 Error

I am unable to subscribe to SAP Build Work Zone, standard edition in my SAP BTP Trial subaccount in the US10 region.

I have completed the following configuration:

  • SAP Cloud Identity Services subscription is active.

  • OIDC trust between the BTP subaccount and the Identity Authentication tenant is active.

  • An Admin group was created in Identity Authentication.

  • The Launchpad_Admin role collection was mapped using Groups equals Admin.

entry.title: Fiori Elements app (OData V4 RAP) on CF managed approuter returns 401 on $metadata - ABAP trial, Wor
entry.content:
Setup: BTP trial, ABAP environment (default_abap-trial), SAP Build Work Zone
standard. App generated in BAS (Fiori Elements LROP, OData V4), deployed with
MTA to CF (managed approuter, html5 repo). Subaccount destination
abap-cloud-default_abap-trial-<subaccount> (OAuth2UserTokenExchange, generated
by BAS). xs-app.json route ^/sap/(.*)$ -> that destination, authenticationType xsuaa.

What works: BAS preview, direct ABAP URL /sap/bc/ui5_ui5/sap/<app>/index.html,
tile shows in the Work Zone site.

What fails: opening the app from Work Zone (or from HTML5 Applications in
cockpit): GET .../sap/opu/odata4/sap/<binding>/srvd/sap/<service>/0001/$metadata
returns 401 and the browser shows a Basic auth popup. Destination client
id/secret re-entered from a fresh service key, no change.

Question: is a CF-deployed app reaching an ABAP environment trial service
supported with OAuth2UserTokenExchange, and what is missing?
